name: temp-accuracy-mc
description: Issue #15's Monte Carlo local-mismatch sweep of design/temp_core.spice (idealised 500 nA IBIAS, same cell-level DUT sim/temp-core-designer-check/ uses): PNP pair/ratio, resistor-ratio and amplifier-offset mismatch contribution to #temp-accuracy-untrimmed and #temp-accuracy-trimmed, at the row's own binding points (temperature extremes x rail extremes). Process held at the deterministic 'tt' corner per binding point -- global process spread is #13's deterministic corner-sweep job; this experiment adds the local-mismatch axis on top, per spec/target-spec.md section 2's [3sigma] definition. POST-LAYOUT SIBLING (issue #83, part of #18): identical to sim/temp-accuracy-mc/testbench/tb.json except that 'netlist' names the fragment sim/build_tb.py assembles from layout/postlayout/temp_core.spice instead of design/netlist/temp_core.spice. The stimulus is shared with the schematic sibling (same DUT ports), and that sibling's manifest, fragment and records are untouched.
claim: POST-LAYOUT RE-RUN (issue #83, part of #18) of the schematic-level record 20260802-082345-989ce7a in sim/temp-accuracy-mc/records/, same stimulus and same checks, DUT swapped from design/netlist/temp_core.spice to layout/postlayout/temp_core.spice. Any check that flips from PASS on that record to FAIL here is a REGRESSION to flag and route to its owning design issue, not to absorb -- the schematic-vs-extracted comparison is generated by sim/postlayout_delta.py into the paired <record-id>-postlayout-delta derived record. The original claim, unchanged, follows. --- spec/target-spec.md#temp-accuracy-untrimmed, #temp-accuracy-trimmed -- local-mismatch share, Monte Carlo, N>=500 per binding point, evaluated at the temperature/rail extremes the rows themselves name as binding. Complements the deterministic systematic/corner share published by sim/temp-accuracy-vt/ (#13).
netlist_provenance_note: layout/postlayout/temp_core.spice's own header (layout/postlayout/AUDIT.md): 114 drawn devices (27 nfet_03v3, 28 pfet_03v3, 9 pnp_10p00x10p00, 50 ppolyf_u) with first-order interconnect R/C on 69/73 nets (138 parasitic cards, sigma R = 65734 ohm, sigma C = 1552.3 fF), net names restored through klt lvs's own 73/73 net correspondence. NOT from the layout: (a) 4 body/well/plate nets (NW1 -> VDD, NW2 -> NT, NWQ -> VSS, vsubs -> VSS) tied to the net the SCHEMATIC puts them on -- the extraction deck's connectivity stack does not reach an Nwell, a substrate ring or a bipolar base well, so they extract isolated and would otherwise float; (b) XCC (cap_mim_2f0_m3m4_noshield, 12u x 12u on PG/NZ) is NOT DRAWN -- reserved floor area -- and is spliced in ideal, so anything in this record that turns on the amplifier's compensation pole is a schematic claim, not a post-layout one. Everything else -- MOS, vertical PNP and poly resistor bodies alike -- is a real extraction of drawn geometry, and this cell needs none of the device-model substitutions AUDIT.md records for the cells that use ppolyf_u_1k or MiM caps.

terr_untrim_c.description: spec/target-spec.md#temp-accuracy-untrimmed ([3sigma], +/-3 C). Untrimmed error against the declared nominal K0=4.308842 mV/K, WITH local mismatch on (sw_stat_mismatch=1) -- this is the mismatch-inclusive counterpart to sim/temp-accuracy-vt/'s deterministic-corners-only terr_untrim_c check.

terr_trim_c.description: spec/target-spec.md#temp-accuracy-trimmed ([3sigma] stretch, +/-1.5 C). DERIVED per-sample (montecarlo.derive_temp_trim): each die's own 25 C reading stands in for a real one-point 25 C production trim on that same die -- see sim/temp-accuracy-mc/testbench/stimulus.spice and sim/harness/montecarlo.py's derive_temp_trim docstring for the full method, which mirrors sim/temp-accuracy-vt/analyze_derived.py's deterministic-grid derivation.
